newsitem.title: UK: Citibank voted best bank in FX Week awards.
newsitem.headline: Citibank voted best bank in FX Week awards.

text.p: Citibank won seven of the 27 best bank awards at this year's FX Week/Syntegra foreign exchange awards, including best bank overall for the second year running.
The awards, based on returns by Treasurers and chief dealers from more than 300 banks worldwide, were presented by U.K. Treasury minister Angela Knight at a reception in London.
Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) was runner up for best overall bank with Chemical Bank third and BankAmerica fourth. The poll was carried out before the Chase/Chemical merger.
FX Week is a weekly magazine devoted to the foreign exchange industry and Syntegra is the systems integration business of British Telecom.
Citibank was also voted best bank in interbank and best bank in New York with Chemical best bank in London, UBS best in Singapore and Bank of Tokyo best bank in Tokyo.
"I think it is significant that these awards are being presented in London," Knight said.
"Not only is London the financial capital in Europe it is the financial gateway of the world," she added.
For currency pairs, Citibank was voted best in dollar/mark with National Westminster Bank Plc best for cable and Bank of Tokyo for dollar/yen.
MW Marshall scored as best broker in London and New York, with Tullett and Tokyo coming second in London and Harlow Meyer in New York.
On the options side, SBC took first place for plain- vanilla and exotic option with Citibank second for both.

Reuters was judged best vendor for forex prices and best electronic news service, with Dow Jones Telerate in second and Knight-Ridder Financial in third. Best forex matching service was Reuters Dealing 2000-2, with Electronic Broking Service (EBS) second.
MMS International was voted the best screen based analytical commentary with last year's winner MCM CurrencyWatch the runner up.
